Definition

Soft iron moves toward stronger magnetic field or two magnetised vanes repel,creating deflection.

Classification / representative type

  • Attraction type and repulsion type;both are secondary indicating instruments,suitable for AC/DCunder their rated conditions.

Construction — part and purpose

  1. Fixed current-carrying coil produces the measuring field;its conductor size/turns depend on ammeter or voltmeter duty.
  2. Soft-iron vane(s)of low-hysteresis material provide the moving magnetic element.
  3. Spindle,bearings and pointer convert vane motion into scale indication with minimal friction.
  4. Controlling spring or approved gravity arrangement produces restoring torque.
  5. Air-friction damping and its chamber settle the pointer;permanent-magnet damping could disturb the measuring field.
  6. Magnetic shielding,scale and enclosure reduce stray-field error and protect the movement.

Working — sequence and reason

  1. Coil current establishes a field and magnetises the iron.
  2. Attraction moves iron into the field;repulsion separates similarly magnetised vanes.
  3. Current reversal reverses both magnetisations,so torque retains its direction.
  4. Average torque depends on mean square current,approximately Td=(1/2)Irms²(dL/dθ).
  5. At equilibrium restoring torque balances deflection;the scale is generally nonlinear/crowded near zero.
  6. Read in the marked position at rated frequency;hysteresis,frequency,stray fields and friction affect accuracy.

Applications

Use only within the stated quantity,range,frequency and waveform limits.

Limitations and safety

RMSresponse is limited by actual frequency/waveform design;do not assume universal true-RMSperformance.

Definition

Acurrent-carrying moving coil experiences torque in the permanent magnet radial field.

Classification / representative type

  • Permanent-magnet moving-coil,DCindicating movement;rectifier-ACinstruments are a modified measurement system.

Construction — part and purpose

  1. Permanent magnet and shaped pole shoes produce an approximately uniform radial field.
  2. Soft-iron cylindrical core reduces reluctance and helps maintain radial flux.
  3. Light insulated copper coil has Nturns and area A,carried on a light former.
  4. Spirally wound control springs provide restoring torque and usually current connections.
  5. Spindle or taut-band suspension,pointer and uniform scale provide indication.
  6. Conducting former/appropriate eddy-current damping produces fast settling without changing the ideal steady reading.

Working — sequence and reason

  1. DCcurrent enters the coil through its connection system.
  2. Opposite active sides experience opposite forces,forming a couple.
  3. Radial field keeps the torque coefficient approximately independent of deflection.
  4. Pointer moves until spring torque balances coil torque.
  5. Damping opposes motion and settles the pointer.
  6. Direct ACproduces reversing torque and nearly zero mean indication;DCpolarity is important.

Applications

Use only within the stated quantity,range,frequency and waveform limits.

Limitations and safety

Sensitive movement needs shunt/multiplier protection.Temperature,magnet ageing and overload can change calibration.

body.en:
Definition

Magnetic interaction between fixed and moving current coils produces torque without a permanent magnet.

Classification / representative type

  • Ammeter,voltmeter or wattmeter connections;an air-cored transfer-type principle can operate on AC/DCwithin ratings.

Construction — part and purpose

  1. Fixed coil(s)produce the current-related magnetic field.
  2. Moving coil on a light support interacts with the fixed-coil field.
  3. Control springs provide return torque and moving-coil connections.
  4. Air-friction damping settles motion without a permanent magnet disturbing the field.
  5. Pointer,scale and low-friction bearings/suspension provide indication.
  6. Wattmeter design uses a heavy current coil and high-resistance pressure-coil circuit with appropriate insulation.

Working — sequence and reason

  1. Current in each coil establishes a magnetic field.
  2. Interaction tends to increase mutual inductance,producing Td=i1i2(dM/dθ).
  3. For AC,the average of the product determines deflection,not the product of independent scalar averages.
  4. For current/voltage indication,the configured coil currents produce an approximately square-law scale.
  5. For wattmetry,a current-proportional coil and voltage-proportional in-phase pressure current yield torque proportional to VIcosφ.
  6. Equilibrium and damping provide a stable reading;frequency/pressure-coil phase and connection losses need attention.

Applications

Use only within the stated quantity,range,frequency and waveform limits.

Limitations and safety

Pressure coil needs rated series resistance;stray fields and low-pfphase errors matter.Never use an arbitrary wiring reversal to recover a negative reading while live.

body.en:
Definition

An ACinduction mechanism turns a disc at speed proportional to real power and counts revolutions as energy.

Classification / representative type

  • Single-phase meter;three-phase meters use appropriate two-element three-wire or three-element four-wire arrangements.

Construction — part and purpose

  1. Series/current magnet carries load current and produces its flux.
  2. Shunt/pressure magnet is connected across the voltage through the designed high-inductance circuit.
  3. Phase-adjusting/shading arrangements set the required flux relationship.
  4. Aluminium disc cuts alternating fluxes;induced eddy currents develop driving torque.
  5. Permanent braking magnet produces speed-dependent opposing torque.
  6. Spindle,bearings and register/gearing count disc revolutions;anti-creep provisions prevent false no-load rotation.

Working — sequence and reason

  1. Voltage and current circuits create time-displaced alternating fluxes.
  2. Disc eddy currents interact with these fluxes to give average driving torque proportional to real power.
  3. Braking torque rises with disc speed.
  4. Steady speed occurs when driving and braking torques balance.
  5. Integrating speed over time gives total revolutions proportional to electrical energy.
  6. Read register units and meter constant carefully;kWhis energy,not kW.Creeping,friction,phase error and overload affect registration.

Applications

Use only within the stated quantity,range,frequency and waveform limits.

Limitations and safety

Only ACand rated frequency/wiring;no student adjustment of seals,braking magnets or revenue-meter settings.

Given and assumptions

Step-by-step solution

  1. At steady speed,kdP=kb n,so n=(kd/kb)P.
  2. Integrate:N=∫n dt=(kd/kb)∫P dt;therefore total revolutions are proportional to energy.
  3. With K rev/kWh,indicated energy Eind=N/K kWh.Expected N=K P(W)t(s)/3600000.
  4. Example:K1200rev/kWh,P1000W,t60s gives20revolutions.

The torque/speed model neglects starting friction and transient effects;use actual nameplate constants and test method.

body.en:
Understand the idea

Different instruments answer different questions even when they share voltage/current inputs.

Explanation and application

  • Maximum demand is the highest demand calculated over the configured integration intervals,not an instantaneous current peak.Interval examples such as15or30minutes are configuration-dependent,not a universal syllabus rule.
  • Trivector instruments register active/reactive/apparent quantities or energies according to their model.kVAhgenerally integrates apparent power;do not always calculate it as√(kWh²+kvarh²)under changing pf.
  • Phase-sequence indicators identify order RYB/RBYusing a rated rotating/electronic principle;they do not prove that a circuit is dead or establish transformer clock displacement.
  • Solid-state meters sense voltage/current,sample/process power and accumulate energy or pulses.They have no disc but still require correct wiring,ratio configuration and calibration.

Given and assumptions

Movement resistance Rm,full-scale current Im;required full-scale line current I>Im.Shunt Rshis parallel to movement.

Step-by-step solution

  1. At full scale,the movement carries Imand the shunt carries Ish=I−Im.
  2. Parallel branches have equal voltage:ImRm=(I−Im)Rsh.
  3. Rearrange:Rsh=ImRm/(I−Im).With multiplying factor m=I/Im,this is Rsh=Rm/(m−1).
  4. Example:Im1mA,Rm100Ω,I1A gives Rsh0.100100Ω.Shunt dissipation at full scale=(I−Im)²Rsh≈0.0999W.

Interpretation and check

Choose a rated stable low-Rshunt,correct connections and thermal margin;an open shunt can overload the movement.The meter remains a series instrument.
